description:
FILED s440 from agent B's #464 report (pre-existing). Runtime module load (p-use / p-require by NAME) must set $INC{"Foo/Bar.pm"} to the path it loaded (a pragma like strict: perl sets it to the real strict.pm path). Bar: `require strict`, `use strict`, `use POSIX ()`, `require Foo::Bar` for a lib/ shim and for a user module via `use lib`, vs perl (exists + the value's shape -- a path); `%INC` after a failed require unchanged; a Pl/t guard row in use-require-01.t.

DONE s443h (Opus, agent H round 4), commit 8cdaeef, ff-merged s444.  ONE mechanism: %p-note-inc-path records-if-absent and resolves through @INC (p-note-inc = module-name face; exported); p-use's three no-load exits call it; p-require-file NOTES instead of clobbering (it used to overwrite p-use's absolute path with the relative one).  Codegen emits (p-note-inc ...) for pragmas via ONE predicate _never_loaded_pragma (the use arm and no arm used to disagree).  p-note-inc loads NOTHING -- hard constraint (would satisfy p-use's already-loaded guard); `no Moose` deliberately not routed, guarded.  Fable re-probed require strict / require "File/Basename.pm" abs-path / failed-require-clean -- identical to perl.  DELIBERATE residue = #528 (constant/vars/lib/base/parent/overload/if record no %INC entry).
subject: `%INC` is not populated by a BAREWORD `require Foo` / `use Foo` -- `require strict; print exists $INC{"strict.pm"} ? 1 : 0` perl 1, PCL 0 (the path form is right); silently breaks the `require Foo unless $INC{"Foo.pm"}` idiom in the other direction
